title: Web Development Foundations
summary: Build a durable foundation in how the web works, semantic HTML, modern CSS, accessibility, responsive design, Git, and JavaScript fundamentals.
description: The recommended starting point for people entering web development or strengthening missing fundamentals. It prioritizes standards, accessibility, practical projects, and clear mental models before frameworks so later tools are easier to understand and evaluate.
outcomes: Build responsive layouts with modern CSS

stages.title: Understand the web and set up tools
stages.summary: Learn how browsers, servers, URLs, files, editors, terminals, and developer tools fit together.
stages.whyItMatters: A clear mental model makes errors easier to diagnose and prevents the browser, terminal, hosting platform, and source files from feeling unrelated.
stages.checkpoint: Explain what happens between entering a URL and seeing a rendered page, then create a local project folder.

project.title: First local webpage
project.brief: Create a small local website, inspect it with browser developer tools, and document how the files, browser, URL, and server would connect when the site is published.

stages.title: Structure content with semantic HTML
stages.summary: Use landmarks, headings, links, lists, media, tables, and forms to describe content accurately.
stages.whyItMatters: Semantic HTML improves accessibility, maintainability, search visibility, keyboard use, and machine understanding.
stages.checkpoint: Build a page that remains understandable without styles and gives every form control an associated label.

project.title: Accessible profile page
project.brief: Build a content-rich profile page whose structure remains clear without CSS, including meaningful landmarks, a logical heading outline, media, links, and a correctly labeled form.

stages.title: Style and lay out interfaces with CSS
stages.summary: Learn the cascade, box model, typography, spacing, Flexbox, Grid, variables, and reusable styles.
stages.whyItMatters: CSS becomes predictable when layout systems and the cascade replace one-off offsets and fixed dimensions.
stages.checkpoint: Rebuild one layout with Flexbox and Grid, then explain which model better represents the relationship.

project.title: Responsive landing page
project.brief: Turn a static content brief into a responsive landing page using reusable spacing and typography tokens, then verify that it remains readable without horizontal overflow.

stages.title: Build responsive and accessible experiences
stages.summary: Design for screen sizes, input methods, contrast needs, text scaling, motion preferences, and assistive technology.
stages.whyItMatters: Accessibility and responsive behavior expose structural product problems and should be quality requirements from the start.
stages.checkpoint: Complete the main flow using only a keyboard at narrow and wide sizes with visible focus.

project.title: Accessibility repair pass
project.brief: Audit an existing page and repair its keyboard flow, focus states, contrast, text scaling, responsive media, and reduced-motion behavior, recording each issue and fix.

stages.title: Add behavior with JavaScript
stages.summary: Learn values, functions, arrays, objects, conditions, modules, DOM events, and simple asynchronous work.
stages.whyItMatters: Strong language fundamentals make frameworks easier and help JavaScript enhance a sound document instead of replacing structure.
stages.checkpoint: Build an interaction from a written state model and explain which data changes after each action.

project.title: Interactive task board
project.brief: Build a task board that supports creating, completing, filtering, and persisting items, with clear empty, loading, and error states driven by an explicit state model.

stages.title: Version and publish your work
stages.summary: Use Git snapshots, branches, focused commits, GitHub repositories, pull requests, documentation, and deployment.
stages.whyItMatters: Version control protects work, makes experiments reversible, and introduces the collaboration flow used by software teams.
stages.checkpoint: Create a branch, make focused commits, merge through a pull request, and recover an earlier file version.

project.title: Published portfolio starter
project.brief: Place your portfolio starter in a public repository, develop one improvement on a branch, review it through a pull request, document the project, and publish the result.

finalProject.title: Accessible multi-page portfolio
finalProject.brief: Design, build, test, version, and publish a small site demonstrating semantic structure, responsive CSS, accessible interactions, and clean project documentation.

title: Frontend JavaScript Developer
summary: Move from strong browser fundamentals into TypeScript, React, application state, data fetching, testing, accessibility, performance, and deployment.
description: For learners who can already build responsive websites and write basic JavaScript. The path develops maintainable frontend applications while keeping React grounded in browser, JavaScript, accessibility, and software design fundamentals.
audience: Developers moving from sites to applications
prerequisites: JavaScript functions, arrays, objects, modules, and DOM events
outcomes: Model state and asynchronous data clearly

stages.title: Strengthen modern JavaScript
stages.summary: Deepen scope, closures, modules, immutable updates, promises, async functions, errors, and browser APIs.
stages.whyItMatters: Framework bugs are often JavaScript misunderstandings in disguise, so language fluency simplifies code and debugging.
stages.checkpoint: Refactor a script into modules with explicit inputs, outputs, loading states, and recoverable errors.

project.title: Data dashboard without a framework
project.brief: Build a framework-free dashboard that loads remote data through small modules, transforms it predictably, handles failures, and exposes useful loading and empty states.

stages.title: Model data with TypeScript
stages.summary: Use inference, unions, interfaces, generics, narrowing, utility types, and strict compiler settings.
stages.whyItMatters: TypeScript is most useful when it documents valid states and catches boundary mistakes rather than hiding uncertainty.
stages.checkpoint: Replace an impossible boolean-state combination with a discriminated union and handle every case.

project.title: Typed data client
project.brief: Create a strict TypeScript client around an external data source, validating unknown input at the boundary and keeping application code free from unsafe any casts.

stages.title: Think in React components
stages.summary: Learn component boundaries, props, rendering, events, state, composition, forms, effects, and reusable behavior.
stages.whyItMatters: Good React code begins with a clear component and state model rather than duplicated state or unnecessary effects.
stages.checkpoint: Break a design into components, identify minimal state, and explain which component should own it.

project.title: Searchable product explorer
project.brief: Build a searchable product explorer from reusable React components, keeping state close to its owner and making every control understandable by keyboard and screen reader.

stages.title: Manage application data and state
stages.summary: Separate server data, URL state, form state, and local interface state while handling synchronization deliberately.
stages.whyItMatters: Treating every value as global state creates unnecessary complexity and unreliable navigation or refresh behavior.
stages.checkpoint: Classify every state value and remove state that can be derived from props, URLs, or fetched data.

project.title: Persistent explorer state
project.brief: Extend the explorer so filters are shareable through the URL, favorites persist locally, server data has explicit loading and error handling, and each state category has a documented owner.

stages.title: Test behavior and accessibility
stages.summary: Write focused unit, component, and end-to-end tests around visible behavior, accessible names, and critical flows.
stages.whyItMatters: Tests create confidence when they protect important behavior without depending on implementation details.
stages.checkpoint: Refactor internal component structure while keeping behavior tests passing unchanged.

project.title: Quality gate
project.brief: Protect one critical user journey with focused unit, component, accessibility, and end-to-end tests that assert visible behavior rather than implementation details.

stages.title: Measure, optimize, and deploy
stages.summary: Learn production builds, performance measurement, bundle awareness, images, deployment previews, and release checks.
stages.whyItMatters: Users experience network and deployment conditions, so working locally is not the end of frontend delivery.
stages.checkpoint: Measure before and after one optimization and document the user-facing improvement.

project.title: Production release
project.brief: Prepare the application for release by measuring its main performance costs, improving the largest issues, automating quality checks, and documenting the deployed result.

finalProject.title: Production-ready frontend application
finalProject.brief: Deliver a typed React application that consumes data, supports shareable search, handles every view state, includes behavior tests, and passes accessibility and performance review.

title: Full-Stack JavaScript Developer
summary: Extend frontend skills into Node.js, HTTP APIs, SQL, data modeling, authentication, security, Next.js full-stack patterns, testing, and delivery.
description: A JavaScript-first path that treats backend work as data ownership, validation, authorization, transactions, failure handling, security, testing, and deployment rather than only route handlers.
audience: Frontend developers moving into backend work
outcomes: Use Next.js server and client boundaries

stages.title: Understand Node.js and server execution
stages.summary: Learn the runtime, modules, packages, configuration, asynchronous I/O, processes, files, and logging.
stages.whyItMatters: Backend code runs under different constraints from browser code, so runtime understanding prevents blocking and configuration failures.
stages.checkpoint: Explain event-loop blocking, configuration entry points, and startup failure reporting.

project.title: Node service starter
project.brief: Create a small Node.js service with validated environment configuration, a health endpoint, structured logs, graceful error handling, and scripts for local development and production.

stages.title: Design HTTP APIs and boundaries
stages.summary: Use methods, status codes, validation, pagination, filters, errors, and contracts for predictable APIs.
stages.whyItMatters: An API is a contract used by people and code, so stable semantics matter more than rapidly adding endpoints.
stages.checkpoint: Document valid, invalid, unauthorized, and not-found behavior for one endpoint.

project.title: Resource catalog API
project.brief: Design and implement a resource catalog API with a written contract, validated inputs, consistent errors, filtering, sorting, and cursor or page-based pagination.

stages.title: Model data with SQL and migrations
stages.summary: Learn tables, keys, relations, constraints, queries, indexes, transactions, migrations, and type-safe access.
stages.whyItMatters: Reliable systems depend on database constraints and transaction boundaries, not only current application checks.
stages.checkpoint: Model a many-to-many relation and enforce one important invariant in the database.

project.title: Persistent catalog
project.brief: Persist the catalog in PostgreSQL using a documented relational schema, repeatable migrations, seed data, constraints, useful indexes, and transaction-safe write operations.

stages.title: Implement authentication and authorization
stages.summary: Separate identity from permission while learning sessions, password handling, role checks, secrets, and common attacks.
stages.whyItMatters: A successful login does not prove permission, and missing server authorization is a common security failure.
stages.checkpoint: Write an authorization matrix and prove client-side role changes cannot grant server permission.

project.title: Role-aware catalog
project.brief: Add authentication and role-based authorization to the catalog, documenting which role may perform each action and proving that protected operations fail safely.

stages.title: Compose a full-stack Next.js application
stages.summary: Use layouts, server and client components, route handlers, mutations, caching, validation, and error boundaries deliberately.
stages.whyItMatters: Next.js helps when server and client responsibilities and cache behavior are explicit rather than accidental.
stages.checkpoint: Explain every client boundary and identify data that can stay on the server.

project.title: Integrated catalog product
project.brief: Combine the catalog into a Next.js product with deliberate server and client boundaries, validated mutations, protected actions, cache decisions, and resilient loading and error states.

stages.title: Test, deliver, and operate the system
stages.summary: Cover integration, database, and end-to-end behavior, then automate checks, deploy, monitor, and rehearse recovery.
stages.whyItMatters: Full-stack responsibility includes migrations, configuration, visibility, deployment order, and recovery.
stages.checkpoint: Deploy a compatible migration, verify the critical flow, and document failure recovery.

project.title: Release pipeline
project.brief: Create a release pipeline that runs integration and end-to-end tests, builds a deployable artifact, applies database changes safely, and includes a concise rollback and recovery runbook.

finalProject.title: Team-ready full-stack product
finalProject.brief: Deliver a complete resource product with typed boundaries, relational data, protected operations, resilient errors, automated tests, migrations, and repeatable deployment.

title: React Native Mobile Developer
summary: Translate React and JavaScript experience into native mobile interfaces, navigation, device APIs, offline behavior, testing, performance, and release preparation.
description: For JavaScript and React developers entering mobile work. The path emphasizes native platform conventions, device constraints, permissions, navigation, lifecycle, and release processes that differ from the browser.
audience: JavaScript developers building Android and iOS apps

stages.title: Adopt the mobile mental model
stages.summary: Understand native rendering, platform conventions, touch input, safe areas, lifecycle, permissions, and tooling.
stages.whyItMatters: A mobile app is not a website in a smaller viewport, and platform behavior shapes the product experience.
stages.checkpoint: Explain which behavior comes from React, the native platform, and the application lifecycle.

project.title: Device-ready starter
project.brief: Create a typed React Native starter that runs on a physical device, respects safe areas and platform conventions, and documents the differences from a browser-based React application.

stages.title: Build reusable native interfaces
stages.summary: Use core components, styling, lists, images, forms, keyboard handling, accessibility, and device layouts.
stages.whyItMatters: Mobile interfaces must remain usable under touch, keyboard, text scaling, and different device sizes.
stages.checkpoint: Use a screen reader, large text, keyboard input, and long content without hiding controls.

project.title: Mobile resource browser
project.brief: Build a mobile resource browser with reusable controls, a virtualized list, keyboard-aware forms, responsive layouts, and accessibility labels tested on a real device.

stages.title: Design navigation and application state
stages.summary: Model stacks, tabs, deep links, route parameters, persisted preferences, and server data separately.
stages.whyItMatters: Users expect predictable back behavior, deep links, restored state, and tab history after suspension.
stages.checkpoint: Open a detail screen from a deep link and restore saved filters after restart.

project.title: Navigable catalog
project.brief: Add stack and tab navigation, deep links into resource details, typed route parameters, and persisted favorites while keeping navigation, local, and server state separate.

stages.title: Integrate APIs and device capabilities
stages.summary: Work with network requests, local storage, media, permissions, secure values, and offline-friendly behavior.
stages.whyItMatters: Device capabilities are asynchronous and permission-controlled while mobile networks are intermittent.
stages.checkpoint: Demonstrate granted, denied, unavailable, offline, loading, and failed states.

project.title: Offline collection
project.brief: Build an offline-friendly saved-resource collection that caches useful data, explains permission requests, protects sensitive values, and recovers clearly from failed network operations.

stages.title: Test and improve mobile quality
stages.summary: Use component tests, device checks, performance profiling, accessibility review, and representative network conditions.
stages.whyItMatters: Mobile bugs often depend on device, operating system, lifecycle, permission, network, or build configuration.
stages.checkpoint: Test the critical journey on a real device with large text, slow network, and denied permission.

project.title: Mobile quality pass
project.brief: Test the main mobile flow across representative devices and network conditions, add automated coverage for critical behavior, and record accessibility and performance findings.

stages.title: Prepare production builds and releases
stages.summary: Understand identifiers, configuration, signing, build profiles, store assets, privacy declarations, and staged releases.
stages.whyItMatters: A development build is only one part of mobile delivery; signed artifacts and store requirements need planning.
stages.checkpoint: Produce a reproducible preview build and document every requirement before store submission.

project.title: Release candidate
project.brief: Produce a signed preview build with environment-specific configuration, release notes, privacy information, store assets, and a checklist for staged distribution and rollback.

finalProject.title: Cross-platform mobile companion
finalProject.brief: Build a polished Android and iOS resource companion with native navigation, API data, offline favorites, one device capability, accessible states, and a reproducible preview release.

title: UI/UX and Product Design
summary: Learn visual foundations, user research, information architecture, flows, wireframes, interface design, prototypes, systems, accessibility, and handoff.
description: This path treats product design as problem solving rather than only visual styling. Learners move from evidence and content structure to tested flows, coherent interfaces, reusable systems, and implementation-ready collaboration.
audience: Visual designers moving into digital products

stages.title: Build visual design foundations
stages.summary: Learn hierarchy, typography, spacing, color, contrast, grids, composition, and consistency.
stages.whyItMatters: Every visual decision should make relationships, priority, and available actions easier to understand.
stages.checkpoint: Explain screen hierarchy without color alone and verify a repeatable spacing and type system.

project.title: Interface reconstruction
project.brief: Reconstruct a polished interface from a reference while documenting its hierarchy, type scale, spacing system, grid, color roles, and contrast decisions instead of copying isolated pixels.

stages.title: Research users and frame the problem
stages.summary: Turn assumptions into questions, observe users, identify patterns, and separate evidence from opinion.
stages.whyItMatters: Teams can build a beautiful answer to the wrong problem when needs and constraints are not understood first.
stages.checkpoint: Support the problem statement with concrete observations and identify untested assumptions.

project.title: Small research study
project.brief: Plan and run a small research study around a real user problem, then synthesize observations into evidence-backed themes without presenting assumptions as findings.

stages.title: Create information architecture and flows
stages.summary: Organize content, define navigation, model journeys, map decisions, identify edge cases, and limit scope.
stages.whyItMatters: Clear structure gives screens a shared logic before visual details make changes more expensive.
stages.checkpoint: A new user can identify the start, complete the primary task, recover, and see the next step.

project.title: Resource discovery flow
project.brief: Design the information architecture and primary task flow for discovering a technical resource, including alternate routes, empty states, errors, and recovery points.

stages.title: Wireframe and prototype interactions
stages.summary: Explore multiple low-fidelity solutions, responsive wireframes, interface content, and usability tests.
stages.whyItMatters: Low-fidelity exploration makes structural changes inexpensive and reveals unclear labels early.
stages.checkpoint: A participant completes the primary task and predicts major actions before selecting them.

project.title: Testable path prototype
project.brief: Explore several low-fidelity solutions, turn the strongest direction into a responsive interactive prototype, test it with users, and record the changes supported by evidence.

stages.title: Design reusable and accessible systems
stages.summary: Create tokens, components, variants, states, patterns, keyboard behavior, errors, and documentation.
stages.whyItMatters: A design system helps teams make consistent accessible decisions rather than only storing polished frames.
stages.checkpoint: Document one component so implementation requires no guessing about behavior or states.

project.title: Mini design system
project.brief: Create a compact design system with tokens, reusable components, variants, interaction states, keyboard behavior, validation patterns, and guidance for correct use.

stages.title: Collaborate, hand off, and communicate decisions
stages.summary: Prepare responsive specifications, acceptance criteria, design QA, change notes, and an evidence-led case study.
stages.whyItMatters: Design creates value when a team can build and evaluate it, so decision clarity matters as much as screens.
stages.checkpoint: A developer can identify responsive behavior, reuse, content rules, and acceptance criteria.

project.title: Implementation handoff
project.brief: Prepare an implementation-ready handoff with responsive behavior, acceptance criteria, edge cases, change notes, and a case study that connects decisions to research and outcomes.

finalProject.title: Evidence-led learning platform concept
finalProject.brief: Research, structure, prototype, test, systematize, and hand off an experience that helps a beginner choose a technical learning path and understand the next action.

title: DevOps for Web Developers
summary: Learn the delivery and reliability skills around web applications: environments, CI/CD, containers, deployment, observability, security, incidents, and improvement.
description: This path gives web developers enough operational knowledge to ship safely, diagnose failures, collaborate with platform teams, and design applications that can be configured, monitored, recovered, and improved in real environments.
audience: Teams without a dedicated platform engineer
prerequisites: Experience running a web application locally

stages.title: Understand systems, processes, and networking
stages.summary: Learn processes, ports, files, permissions, environment variables, DNS, HTTP, TLS, and proxies.
stages.whyItMatters: Deployment failures are hard to diagnose when operating system, network, runtime, and application are one black box.
stages.checkpoint: Trace one request from DNS through TLS and a proxy to the application process.

project.title: Request-path diagram
project.brief: Map a web request from browser to application and database, identify every port and configuration boundary, and document the likely symptoms when each dependency fails.

stages.title: Create repeatable builds and environments
stages.summary: Separate source, dependencies, builds, runtime configuration, development, previews, staging, and production.
stages.whyItMatters: Reliable releases come from reproducible inputs and explicit configuration rather than undocumented machine state.
stages.checkpoint: Build the same commit in clean environments and document build-time and runtime values.

project.title: Environment contract
project.brief: Define a reproducible environment contract that separates source, dependencies, build output, runtime configuration, and secrets across development, preview, and production.

stages.title: Automate continuous integration
stages.summary: Run type checks, tests, builds, security checks, and artifacts automatically on focused repository events.
stages.whyItMatters: CI moves important verification from personal memory into a visible repeatable workflow.
stages.checkpoint: Open a failing pull request, locate the failed step, repair it, and confirm deployment waits.

project.title: CI quality pipeline
project.brief: Build a CI workflow that runs only on meaningful repository events, caches dependencies safely, executes required quality checks, and publishes a readable build result.

stages.title: Use containers where they add value
stages.summary: Learn images, layers, Dockerfiles, containers, volumes, networks, registries, Compose, and health checks.
stages.whyItMatters: Containers should solve environment and delivery needs rather than becoming an unexplained extra layer.
stages.checkpoint: Rebuild from a clean cache, run with documented configuration, and explain persistence.

project.title: Containerized application
project.brief: Package an application with a small repeatable image, non-root execution, health checks, persistent data where needed, and a Compose setup for its local dependencies.

stages.title: Deploy safely and observe behavior
stages.summary: Use previews, release ordering, migration discipline, health checks, structured logs, metrics, and alerts.
stages.whyItMatters: A successful deploy command does not prove a healthy product; independent signals must confirm real behavior.
stages.checkpoint: Deploy a change, verify health independently, and distinguish app, network, and dependency errors.

project.title: Observable deployment
project.brief: Design a deployment flow with ordered migrations, health verification, structured logs, actionable metrics, alert thresholds, and a checklist for confirming the release.

stages.title: Improve security, reliability, and incident response
stages.summary: Apply least privilege, secret rotation, dependency review, backups, recovery objectives, incident roles, and learning.
stages.whyItMatters: Failures cannot be eliminated completely, so systems must limit impact, restore service, and convert incidents into improvements.
stages.checkpoint: Run a tabletop incident and document detection, ownership, communication, and recovery.

project.title: Operational readiness pack
project.brief: Create an operational readiness pack covering least privilege, secret rotation, dependency review, backups, recovery objectives, incident ownership, communication, and post-incident learning.

finalProject.title: Reliable delivery system
finalProject.brief: Take an application from local-only operation to a documented, reproducible, automatically checked, container-ready, observable deployment with a tested recovery process.
